"summary": "Attempt t-194 changed nothing: the diff is 0 bytes and applies cleanly. All 15 evidence copies re-hash to their sealed sha256, and the four exported events verify against their event-chain hashes. Events 83041 and 83131 record accepted false, outcome regression, verdict FAIL, equal champion and attempt score, tamper PASS at all seven points, and audit 83114 is PASS with no flags. Every claim is supported.",

{"id": "s1", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83131", "observed": "attempt event 83131 matches its chain hash: run rr-004, key rr-004:r1:s0, verdict FAIL (rejected), outcome regression, accept_event 83041, tamper PASS over 7 points, 4 gates"}],

 "note": "Summary claim read from event 83131; its FAIL verdict with accepted false is what the report calls rejected. I could not count ledger rows outside the packet, so the once part rests on the single exported attempt event."},
{"id": "r1", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,

 "note": "The frozen command compiles packs/refpack-toyzip/toyzip.py with python3 -B -c compile(); it does real work and the fresh run passed."},
{"id": "r2", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "g-source", "observed": "gate source re-run on tree: rc 0, PASS, log 'source gate passed (2661 bytes)', sha equals sealed 0b107551"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The source check could be loosened in the frozen contract so it passes on any source; this run only shows it passed under the contract as frozen.",
 "note": "Re-ran the frozen source_check.py gate through bin/rerun; fresh result PASS matches the claim."},
{"id": "r3", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "g-unit", "observed": "gate unit re-run on tree: rc 0, PASS, '22 cases passed', log sha equals sealed ab425529"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The corpus holds only 22 cases, so a defect outside those inputs would not show and the unit gate would still pass.",
 "note": "Re-ran the frozen unit_tests.py gate; all 22 corpus cases printed PASS."},
{"id": "r4", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "g-metric", "observed": "gate metric:total_bytes re-run on tree: rc 0, PASS, 'METRIC: total_bytes 101578'"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The metric gate passes whenever measure.py prints a number, so PASS says nothing about whether the number improved.",
 "note": "Re-ran the frozen measure.py gate. The result block carries a per-run nonce that differs between runs, as expected; the value 101578 is the same."},
{"id": "r5", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "g-metric2", "observed": "second fresh metric run: total_bytes 101578, rc 0"}, {"receipt": "g-metric3", "observed": "third fresh metric run: total_bytes 101578, rc 0; with g-metric that makes three runs, all 101578"}, {"receipt": "ev-83131", "observed": "event metrics total_bytes median 101578.0, n_ok 3, repeats [101578.0 x3]"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The median is correct only if repeats were not cherry-picked: more than three repeats may have run, with the failed ones dropped from n_ok.",
 "note": "Three fresh runs I made all gave 101578, matching the recorded repeats and median."},

 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83041", "observed": "accept event 83041: phase deficit, accepted false, outcome regression, score -0.15429545 equal to champion_score -0.15429545, same reason text as the claim"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The accept rule is wrong to call an exact tie a regression, so a correct rule would accept the attempt; this check reads the recorded decision, not the rule.",
 "note": "I did not re-run the accept rule, which has no shell command in the packet; I read the hash-checked accept event."},
{"id": "r7", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83131", "observed": "event diff block: path .alpaca/research/rr-004/attempts/t-194/attempt.diff, bytes 0, empty true, sha e3b0c442..."}, {"receipt": "apply", "observed": "applying packet/diff.patch (0 bytes) with git apply --allow-empty gave rc 0"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The recorded diff file differs from the attempt tree's real change, so the tree was edited without it showing; the audit fingerprint rules this out only if sound.",
 "note": "packet/diff.patch is 0 bytes and its sha256 e3b0c442... is the empty-input digest."},
{"id": "r8", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83131", "observed": "attempt event: verdict FAIL, outcome regression, reason 'deficit score ... does not rise over the champion's'"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The word rejected is the report's own rendering of FAIL; a reader could take rejected to mean the champion was changed or an owner action, which the event does not show.",
 "note": "The record says verdict FAIL, accepted false, outcome regression; I read FAIL with accepted false as rejected."},
{"id": "h1", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "g-build", "observed": "build gate rerun, rc 0 PASS"}, {"receipt": "g-source", "observed": "source gate rerun, rc 0 PASS"}, {"receipt": "g-unit", "observed": "unit gate rerun, rc 0 PASS, 22 cases"}, {"receipt": "g-metric", "observed": "metric:total_bytes gate rerun, rc 0 PASS, 101578"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The reproduce blocks show commands with unexpanded variables, so a different CONTRACT_DIR or corpus on another machine could make a re-run behave differently.",
 "note": "Each of the four gate items ran through bin/rerun --gate --side tree in the offline jail. The commands do the work their claims state: compile, source check, 22-case unit run, and byte measurement."},
{"id": "e1", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e1", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/01-attempt-1-1.log matches sealed 06095963..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The build gate log holds only the jail-start line, so the copy can match its hash while telling little about the build.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched the sealed sha256."},
{"id": "e2", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e2", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/02-attempt-1-1.log matches sealed 0b107551..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The source log copy was swapped for a different log with the same sealed digest recorded, which only a hash collision allows.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched the sealed sha256."},
{"id": "e3", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e3", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/03-attempt-1-1.log matches sealed ab425529..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The unit log copy is stale and the original in the repository changed after seal; the sealed digest would then not match the live file.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched the sealed sha256."},
{"id": "e4", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e4", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/04-attempt-1-3.log matches sealed d4fdd349..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The metric log is only the third repeat, so a hash match says nothing about repeats one and two.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched the sealed sha256. The log carries a per-run nonce, so my own re-run logs have different hashes; that is expected."},
{"id": "e5", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e5", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/05-open.json matches sealed a1bdd928..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The open fingerprint was taken after the tree was already modified, so a matching hash would seal a wrong baseline.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched; the file names point open, errors empty, taken 18:46:06."},
{"id": "e6", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e6", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/06-after-proposer.json matches sealed c436ac43..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The after-proposer fingerprint omits a path the proposer could write, so an unrecorded write would stay hidden.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched; file names point after-proposer, errors empty."},
{"id": "e7", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e7", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/07-after-implementer.json matches sealed 9aa83b6c..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The after-implementer file was rewritten after sealing and the seal list is stale; the live file would then differ from the copy.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched; file names point after-implementer, errors empty."},
{"id": "e8", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e8", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/08-after-eval.json matches sealed a4935eda..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The after-eval fingerprint was taken before the metric gate wrote its logs, so later tampering would fall outside it.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched; file names point after-eval, errors empty."},
{"id": "e9", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e9", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/09-after-audit.json matches sealed 0cfdd377..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The after-audit point was captured in the same second as after-notes, so a change between the two would go unseen.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched; file names point after-audit, errors empty."},
{"id": "e10", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e10", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/10-after-notes.json matches sealed e3ffe37d..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The notes launch could write outside the fingerprinted set, and this hash would still match its sealed copy.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched; file names point after-notes, errors empty."},
{"id": "e11", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e11", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/11-close.json matches sealed 07245cc7..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The close fingerprint was recorded before the attempt event was written, so state added by closing is not covered.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched; file names point close, errors empty, taken 18:47:31."},
{"id": "e12", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e12", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/12-prompt.txt matches sealed 0b6825a1..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The proposer prompt in the packet is not the prompt the proposer actually received, which a file hash alone cannot show.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched the sealed sha256."},
{"id": "e13", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e13", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/13-prompt.txt matches sealed f0cdca0f..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The implementer prompt copy came from a later regeneration of the launch folder and not from the run itself.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched the sealed sha256."},
{"id": "e14", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e14", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/14-prompt.txt matches sealed 57dda847..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The auditor prompt is 20703 bytes and could hold embedded steering text; a matching hash only proves the file is unchanged.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched the sealed sha256."},
{"id": "e15", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "h-e15", "observed": "re-hash of packet/evidence/15-prompt.txt matches sealed 3c7c8f18..., match true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The notes prompt was edited after launch and the seal was taken from the edited file, so the hash would match the wrong text.",
 "note": "Pointer re-hash matched the sealed sha256."},
{"id": "e16", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83131", "observed": "event 83131 re-verified: hash 72442af9... equals the sealed hash, match true, kind research-attempt"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The attempt event is genuine but a later event supersedes it for t-194, so it is not the final record.",
 "note": "Used the event receipt for this event pointer. The sealed hash is the event-chain hash, so a plain sha256 of the exported file differs (h-e16 shows match false); the event receipt matched."},
{"id": "e17", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83041", "observed": "event 83041 re-verified: hash 78a99140... equals the sealed hash, match true, kind research-accept"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The accept event hash matches but its chain predecessor was altered; the receipt checks the event, not later rewriting of the earlier rows.",
 "note": "Event receipt matched. Sealed value is the event-chain hash, not the file sha256, so h-e17 reports match false by design."},
{"id": "e18", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83114", "observed": "event 83114 re-verified: hash e6838d0a... equals the sealed hash, match true, kind research-audit-verdict"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The audit event hash matches but the audit review it points at was itself shallow; this checks integrity, not audit quality.",
 "note": "Event receipt matched. Sealed value is the event-chain hash, so a plain file sha256 differs by design (h-e18 match false)."},
{"id": "e19", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-82980", "observed": "event 82980 re-verified: hash f13b0d5d... equals the sealed hash, match true, kind research-proposal"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The proposal event is valid but the category it names (better-matches) was never acted on, leaving the attempt empty.",
 "note": "Event receipt matched. Sealed value is the event-chain hash, so a plain file sha256 differs by design (h-e19 match false)."},
{"id": "x1", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "apply", "observed": "git apply --binary --allow-empty ../packet/diff.patch on tree gave rc 0, no output"}, {"read": "packet/diff.patch", "observed": "file is 0 bytes; brief diff_sha256 e3b0c442... is the empty-input digest, engine.empty true"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The applied tree already holds changes absent from the empty patch, so no change on d01a3be8 would not mean the tree equals that head.",
 "note": "Apply receipt exits 0 on the zero-byte patch, as the claim says. base_differs is null and the patch is empty, so base equals tree."},
{"id": "x2", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "g-build", "observed": "build rc 0 PASS"}, {"receipt": "g-source", "observed": "source rc 0 PASS"}, {"receipt": "g-unit", "observed": "unit rc 0 PASS"}, {"receipt": "g-metric", "observed": "metric:total_bytes rc 0 PASS"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The chain order differs from the recorded order (build, source, unit, metric), so a run in another order could hide a dependency; I ran each item alone.",
 "note": "All four gate items re-ran on tree with the same rc and verdict as the recorded chain, and event 83131 lists the same four PASS gates."},
{"id": "m1", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "g-metric", "observed": "metric gate fresh run 1: total_bytes 101578, rc 0"}, {"receipt": "g-metric2", "observed": "fresh run 2: total_bytes 101578"}, {"receipt": "g-metric3", "observed": "fresh run 3: total_bytes 101578"}, {"receipt": "ev-83131", "observed": "recorded repeats [101578.0, 101578.0, 101578.0], median 101578.0, spread 0.0"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The measure is deterministic only on this host; on a different corpus path or Python version the three repeats could differ and the median shift.",
 "note": "Three fresh runs of the metric gate matched the recorded repeats; the median of three equal values is 101578."},
{"id": "x3", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83041", "observed": "accept event: accepted false, outcome regression, score -0.15429545454545454 equals champion_score, margin 0.0, repeats_failed false, untested false"}, {"receipt": "ev-83131", "observed": "attempt metrics and champion_metrics are identical: median 101578.0, repeats [101578.0 x3], spread 0.0"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The champion metrics quoted were taken from a stale champion record, so the tie against them would be a tie against the wrong baseline.",
 "note": "Both events re-verify against their chain hashes and agree with the claim text. I did not re-run the accept rule, as it has no packet command."},
{"id": "x4", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83114", "observed": "audit event 83114 re-verified (match true): verdict PASS, flags [], voided false, breach_toward_attempt false"}, {"read": "packet/audit.json", "observed": "review outcome matches-verdict, one info finding: no tool calls, empty diff, no flags"}],
 "failure_scenario": "The audit verdict PASS reflects an empty transcript only; a real aimed-at-the-checks attempt would need a non-empty one to be judged, so PASS here is weak evidence about audit rigor.",
 "note": "The event's own fields say verdict PASS and flags []; the claim restates them."},
{"id": "x5", "verdict": "supported", "reason": null,
 "evidence": [{"receipt": "ev-83131", "observed": "tamper block: points open, after-proposer, after-implementer, after-eval, after-audit, after-notes, close; verdict PASS"}, {"receipt": "h-e5", "observed": "open fingerprint rehash matches; file names point open with errors []"}, {"receipt": "h-e11", "observed": "close fingerprint rehash matches; point close, errors []"}],
 "failure_scenario": "Per-point PASS is inferred from the event's single overall tamper verdict PASS and empty errors lists, so one point could have a changed entry that the overall verdict missed.",
 "note": "The attempt event lists all seven points with an overall PASS; I read the seven fingerprint copies re-hashed above and each names its point with empty errors. I did not diff the entry maps between points."}
]}
